label: TP
reason: Both alerts are True Positives. The XSS alert is valid because user input from the HTTP header flows through URL decoding, a List manipulation (add/remove/get), and concatenation directly into the SQL string which is then printed to the response writer—bypassing any meaningful sanitization for HTML context. The SQL injection alert is also valid because the same user-controlled data reaches the JDBC execute() sink within the constructed SQL string. Although ESAPI.encodeForHTML is called on the SQL string for display purposes, it does not sanitize the SQL string itself against SQL injection; it only encodes special characters for HTML rendering. Therefore, the underlying SQL remains vulnerable to injection attacks.

evidence.note: User input from request header flows to bar variable, then into SQL string which is both executed (SQLi risk) and printed to response (XSS risk). ESAPI.encodeForHTML is applied to the SQL string for logging/display but does not mitigate the SQL injection vulnerability.
